cards.claim: The NCERT Exemplar defines a linear equation in two variables as one of the form ax + by + c = 0 with a, b, c real and a and b non-zero.
cards.quote: An equation of the form ax + by + c = 0, where a, b and c are real numbers such that a ≠ 0 and b ≠ 0, is called a linear equation in two variables.

cards.claim: A linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions.
cards.quote: Further, a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions.

cards.claim: The graph of every linear equation in two variables is a straight line, and every point on that line represents a solution of the equation.
cards.quote: The graph of every linear equation in two variables is a straight line and every point on the graph (straight line) represents a solution of the linear equation.

cards.claim: A linear relationship between x and y is represented by the straight line y = ax + b, whose slope is a.
cards.quote: A linear relationship between two variables x and y is represented by a straight line y = ax + b. The slope of this line is a.

cards.claim: ax + by + c = 0 is a linear equation in two variables only if both a and b are non-zero; with arbitrary real a, b the statement is false.
cards.quote: (i) False, because ax + by + c = 0 is a linear equation in two variables if both a and b are non-zero.

cards.claim: To find where 3x + 4y = 12 cuts the x-axis, put y = 0: 3x = 12 gives x = 4, so the point is (4, 0).
cards.quote: The graph of the linear equation 3 x + 4 y = 12 cuts the x-axis at the point where y = 0. On putting y = 0 in the linear equation, we have 3 x = 12, which gives x = 4.

cards.claim: Thinking that a linear equation in two variables (such as 2x + 3y = 5) has a unique solution is false: it has infinitely many.
cards.quote: (ii) False, because a linear equation in two variables has infinitely many solutions.
